quote: Proposition 1. Let X1 and X2 be two random variables such that X1 and X2 have the pdfs of the TIIPTL-G family given by f(x; α1, β, ξ) and f(x; α2, β, ξ), respectively. Then, we have X1 ≤lr X2.
family: Type II power Topp-Leone-G (TIIPTL-G): F(x; α, β, ξ) = 1 − [1 − G(x; ξ)]^{αβ} {2 − [1 − G(x; ξ)]^β}^α, with common β and baseline parameter vector ξ; only α differs (α1 vs α2)
compared: shape parameter α1 vs α2 (same β, same baseline G(·; ξ))

hypotheses.text: Let X1 and X2 be two random variables such that X1 and X2 have the pdfs of the TIIPTL-G family given by f(x; α1, β, ξ) and f(x; α2, β, ξ), respectively.
hypotheses.formal: X1 ~ TIIPTL-G(α1, β, ξ), X2 ~ TIIPTL-G(α2, β, ξ)

hypotheses.text: X ≤lr Y if and only if the ratio of the two corresponding pdfs (the one of X divided by the one of Y) is a decreasing function in x
hypotheses.formal: definition of the lr order used

hypotheses.text: [proof shows] [log f(x;α1,β,ξ)/f(x;α2,β,ξ)]' = 2β(α2 − α1)·g(x;ξ)(1−[1−G(x;ξ)]^β)/((1−G(x;ξ))(2−[1−G(x;ξ)]^β)), 'which is negative if α2 < α1'
hypotheses.formal: the proof actually establishes the lr order only under α2 < α1, i.e. α1 > α2

conclusion.direction: X1 <=lr X2 (as printed); per the proof this holds when α1 > α2

quantifiers: α, β > 0, x ∈ R; no explicit range restriction
ambiguity: The printed statement asserts X1 ≤lr X2 without any hypothesis relating α1 and α2; the proof only derives the decreasing likelihood ratio 'if α2 < α1'. The required condition α1 > α2 is missing from the statement as printed.
